name: Subtiaba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Lehmann, Walter. 1920. Zentral-Amerika, Teil I (Subtiaba grammar sketch); also Campbell, Lyle. 1997. American Indian Languages (notes on Subtiaba). Neither full text reachable online.

sources.citation: Sapir, Edward. 1925. The Hokan affinity of Subtiaba in Nicaragua. American Anthropologist n.s. 27(3): 402-435 [part 1].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: p. 405: 'The orthography has been slightly simplified and normalized.. Stress accents have been omitted.' p. 426 (II. Notes on Subtiaba Phonology): 'It is not my purpose to discuss Subtiaba phonetics in any detail, nor would Dr. Lehmann's somewhat inadequate orthography make it possible to do so in any event.' p. 407 no. 93 notes Lehmann accents 'raw' ma"ca' vs 'green' ma'ca' ('perhaps of tone'). 'Accented/unaccented' vowels appear only in diachronic vowel-loss arguments (pp. 429, 433-435). No statement of where word stress falls.

sources.citation: Lehmann, Walter. 1915. Über die Stellung und Verwandtschaft der Subtiaba-Sprache der pazifischen Küste Nicaraguas und über die Sprache von Tapachula in Süd-Chiapas. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 47: 1-34.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classificatory/comparative article (Subtiaba ~ Tlapanec, and wider Oaxacan comparisons) with word lists; scanned text of pp. 1-34 contains no remark on Betonung/Akzent/stress.

sources.citation: Radin, Paul. 1933. Notes on the Tlappanecan language of Guerrero. IJAL 8(1): 45-72.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tlapanec pitch-tone description; Subtiaba forms are quoted from Lehmann 1920 Bd. II pp. 919-968 for comparison only; no statement about Subtiaba stress.

sources.citation: Sapir, Edward. 1925. The Hokan affinity of Subtiaba in Nicaragua (conclusion). American Anthropologist n.s. 27(4): 491-527.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Morphology only. p. 494 fn. 11 distrusts Lehmann's vowel quantities ('Many German (and English) investigators have a tendency to consider all close vowels long, particularly if they occur in an open syllable and bear the stress'). Nothing on stress placement.
